changelog: Replace C1 to keep the contradiction check but forbid fixing it by promoting an adjacent cut that yields a head-fragment; prefer cuts that preserve a minimal meaningful phrase — addresses the primary finding that demoting contradicting remainders caused harmful one-word/head-fragment pieces.

Insert a new principle after C1 allowing isolation of an initial function word or discourse marker when the remainder is a cohesive, self-contained clause — responds to the critique that early opener cuts can be safe and helpful in very-short latency bins.

Replace C5 to allow isolating sentence-initial function words or discourse markers when the following piece is cohesive and non-contradictory — addresses the primary finding that early opener cuts can be safe and useful in very-short latency bins.
Replace E1 with labeled example en_us_845 to expose a measured case where demoting contradicting remainders produced harmful head-fragment cuts in short latency bins.
Replace E2 with labeled example en_us_738 to teach the scorer about subject–auxiliary and tiny-remainder harms evidenced in ≤3 bin failures.
Replace E3 with labeled example en_us_936 to show a case where isolating/opening function words was beneficial and to contrast safe opener cuts with harmful head-fragments.
Replace E4 with labeled example en_us_113 to illustrate contradictions-from-short-remainders that the policy should avoid promoting into one-word/head-fragment pieces.

Replace C8 to keep the clause-closure/cohesion check but explicitly allow isolating sentence-initial function words or discourse markers when the remainder is a cohesive, self-contained clause and the isolated opener does not itself assert a contradicting proposition — addresses the primary finding about safe opener cuts in very-short latency bins.
